clue.text: Prominent man venerated when hosting immigrant

indicators.note: a host has guests inside the house, so one piece takes the other within it

blocks.note: a saint is a venerated person, abbreviated ST
an alien is someone from another country

explanation.surface: A well-known figure, revered by many, takes in a newcomer from abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man venerated' reads as a description of the prominent man, but it is just the saint abbreviation, opened up to take the foreigner.
explanation.definitionFit: Salient describes a feature that stands out or is most noticeable, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Remove clothes, bare bottom and streak!

indicators.note: in a down entry the bottom of a word is its final letter, so only that one is kept

blocks.note: to strip is to undress
the last letter of bare

explanation.surface: An instruction to undress and go streaking with a bare bottom.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface sets up streaking as running naked; the definition takes 'streak' as a line of colour instead.
explanation.definitionFit: A streak of colour is a narrow band or line, which is what a stripe is.

clue.text: Perhaps pups make a mess

blocks.note: first meaning: the young born to one animal at one time, puppies being an example
second meaning: rubbish scattered untidily about

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests puppies being messy; in fact the word means both the brood and the scattered rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: A dog gives birth to a litter of young, and litter is also discarded rubbish left lying around.

clue.text: Sexed-up face of obnoxious jerk is consumed by rampant lust

indicators.note: the face is the front, so only the opening letter is wanted from the next word
what is consumed ends up inside the consumer, so one piece sits within the other
rampant means running wild and unchecked, so these letters run riot into a new order

blocks.note: the first letter of obnoxious
a tic is an involuntary jerk or twitch
lust is strong desire

explanation.surface: A lurid tabloid tale of a nasty man's face twitching with unbridled lust.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lust' must first be turned into a six-letter synonym before the anagram works; the shuffled letters then split to wrap round the face and the jerk.
explanation.definitionFit: To sex something up is to make it more sexual, which is exactly what eroticised means as an adjective.

clue.text: What a steak - packed with flavour!

indicators.note: something packed with contents holds them inside, so the letters sit within the words

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of the first word, the whole second and the start of the third

explanation.surface: An exclamation of delight at a really tasty piece of beef.
explanation.walkthrough: The dash makes it read as one cry of praise; the answer is tucked inside the first three words.
explanation.definitionFit: Taste and flavour are direct synonyms for the sensation food gives the palate.

clue.text: Sights if front of lens held backwards?

definitions.text: Sights if front of lens held backwards?

indicators.note: the front of a word is its first letter, so only that one is taken
going backwards means the letters are read in the opposite direction
what is held is gripped inside something else, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: to sight something is to see it
taken as written
the first letter of lens

explanation.surface: A puzzled musing on what you see when a camera faces the wrong way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sights' is a verb here, not the noun it seems. The whole clue also describes the answer: photos taken with the camera turned back on yourself.
explanation.definitionFit: A selfie is a photograph taken of oneself by pointing the phone's lens back at the photographer.

clue.text: Something to control mood or tension when agitated

indicators.note: agitated means shaken up and disturbed, so the letters are stirred into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Advice on calming yourself when stressed, as if recommending a remedy for nerves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mood or tension' reads as a single pair of feelings, but the split comes after mood and 'or tension' is the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Serotonin is a neurotransmitter in the brain that helps regulate mood, so it is a chemical example of the definition.

clue.text: Head scan moving right to left

indicators.note: the abbreviations for right and left are swapped, so one letter is exchanged for the other

blocks.note: to scan a text is to read it

explanation.surface: A medical image of the skull taken in a sweep from one side to the other.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Right to left' sounds like the direction of a scan or a reversal, but it means R becomes L in the word for scan.
explanation.definitionFit: To head a group is to lead it, as a verb meaning to be in charge or in front.

clue.text: Skill in sport mainly raised local business connections

indicators.note: mainly means most but not all, so the final letter is dropped
to be in something is to sit inside it, so one piece goes within the other
in a down entry raising letters makes them read from the bottom up

blocks.note: art is skill, as in the art of persuasion
tennis is a sport; only its first five letters are used

explanation.surface: Someone talented at a game boosted their local networking for business.
explanation.walkthrough: ART goes inside TENNI, and the whole of TENARTNI is then read upward.
explanation.definitionFit: An intranet is a private computer network linking the staff of one organisation, unlike the public internet.

clue.text: Report of illness: East hit initially - Covid is returning

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the opening letter is kept
returning means going back, so the letters are read in the opposite direction

blocks.note: E is the abbreviation for east
to tonk is British slang for hitting hard, especially a ball in cricket
the first letter of Covid
taken as written

explanation.surface: A news report that a virus wave has struck the east of the country again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Initially' belongs to Covid, not hit; tonk is an informal British word for a hard hit. The four pieces are then read upward.
explanation.definitionFit: A sick note is a certificate from a doctor stating that someone is too ill to work.

clue.text: Correspondence has neither start nor end in address

indicators.note: with neither first nor last letter, the word is trimmed at both sides

blocks.note: an address is a formal speech, an oration

explanation.surface: A letter that lacks an opening greeting and a sign-off at the address.
explanation.walkthrough: Correspondence and address both suggest letters and post; here address is a speech and correspondence a proportion.
explanation.definitionFit: Correspondence can mean a matching relationship between quantities, which is what a ratio expresses mathematically.

clue.text: Pole’s a cold place to be drinking when scoffing!

indicators.note: a drinker takes liquid inside, so one piece swallows the other

blocks.note: S for the south pole; the 's simply joins it on
the Arctic is a famously cold region
as can mean when, as in 'as I arrived'

explanation.surface: A jibe that a Polish person sees the frozen north as a fine place for drinking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pole' suggests a person from Poland, but it is just the compass pole S; 'scoffing' looks like eating, but means mocking.
explanation.definitionFit: Scoffing means mocking or jeering, and a sarcastic remark is a mocking one.

clue.text: Papers with coverage of 'Freebies for Leaders' …

indicators.note: to have coverage is to be covered over, so one piece is wrapped round the other

blocks.note: ID means identity papers
presents are gifts, given free

explanation.surface: Newspapers covering a story about perks handed to politicians, set up as a headline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Papers' suggests newspapers but is the ID abbreviation for identity documents. The quotes make the headline look like one unit, but it splits into wordplay and definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A president is the head of a state or organisation, so presidents are leaders.

clue.text: … reflected new light in story

indicators.note: a reflection in a mirror shows things the other way round

blocks.note: N is the abbreviation for new
a ray is a beam of light

explanation.surface: Continuing the newspaper story: the press casts fresh light on the tale.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links this to the previous clue's surface but the wordplay is self-contained.
explanation.definitionFit: A yarn is an informal word for a tale, often a long or embellished one.

clue.text: Layperson runs off amidst uproar, leading to church separation

indicators.note: when something goes off it leaves, so a letter departs
amidst means in the middle of, so one piece sits inside the other

blocks.note: a din is a loud uproar
a verger is a lay official who looks after a church
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A lay member storms out amid a row, causing a split in the congregation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Church separation' reads as a single schism, but church only supplies the abbreviation for the Church of England at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Divergence is a moving apart or parting of ways, so it is a near synonym for separation.

clue.text: Popular region - desperate to go!

blocks.note: in means fashionable or popular
a continent is a large region of the world

explanation.surface: A holiday advert for a sought-after destination that everyone is longing to visit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Desperate to go' sounds like travel lust; it means urgently needing the toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: Incontinent means unable to control the bladder, a humorous stretch for someone who urgently needs a lavatory.

clue.text: State head invests approximately nothing - that might lead to grounds for bitterness

definitions.text: that might lead to grounds for bitterness

indicators.note: to invest is to put something into something else, so one piece is placed inside

blocks.note: CA is the postal abbreviation for California
ca is the abbreviation for circa, meaning about
O looks like zero
bean is slang for the head

explanation.surface: A national leader puts almost no money in, which could give people reason to feel resentful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'State head' looks like a president; instead the state and the head are split apart to take in the other two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: The seed of the cacao tree is roasted and ground to make cocoa, which is bitter unless sweetened.

clue.text: Force old boy to keep an eye on ticker

blocks.note: F is the physics symbol for force
OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil
to watch is to keep an eye on

explanation.surface: Making an elderly man monitor his heart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ticker' suggests the heart, given the old boy; here it is an informal word for a clock or watch.
explanation.definitionFit: Ticker is informal for a timepiece, and a fob watch is a pocket watch worn on a chain.

clue.text: Loose Women rap human resources

indicators.note: loose means not fixed in place, so these letters can be freely rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: The cast of Loose Women, a British daytime TV chat show, take up rapping about personnel.
explanation.walkthrough: The italic title makes 'Loose Women' look like one name; 'Loose' is the anagram signal for the next two words.
explanation.definitionFit: Manpower is the number of people available for work, the same workforce sense as human resources.

clue.text: At heart of stone, when cut, light's an intrinsic quality, they say

definitions.text: At heart of stone, when cut, light's an intrinsic quality, they say

indicators.note: what people say is heard rather than read, so the sound matters, not the spelling

blocks.note: an opal is a gemstone
the essence of something is its intrinsic nature

explanation.surface: A jeweller's remark that a cut gem's inner glow is part of its nature.
explanation.walkthrough: Heard aloud, 'opal essence' — the heart or essence of the stone — runs together as one word. The whole clue also describes the milky play of light inside a cut opal.
explanation.definitionFit: Opalescence is the milky, shifting iridescence seen in opals, the light that is inherent to the cut stone.

clue.text: Peter for one ruled heartlessly in retrospect

indicators.note: without a heart the middle letter is taken out
retrospect means looking back, so the letters are read the other way

blocks.note: a monarch who ruled reigned

explanation.surface: A historian's harsh verdict on how a Russian tsar Peter governed.
explanation.walkthrough: Peter the Great makes 'ruled' feel like history; but this Peter is the apostle, who denied knowing Jesus three times.
explanation.definitionFit: Saint Peter famously disowned Jesus three times before the cock crowed, making him the Bible's best-known example of one who denies.

clue.text: Sedition - beheaded for cause

indicators.note: losing the head means losing the first letter

blocks.note: sedition is incitement against the state, close to treason

explanation.surface: A traitor executed for their rebellious cause.
explanation.walkthrough: Beheading was the old punishment for treason, so the surface and the deletion share a picture.
explanation.definitionFit: A cause is a ground or motive for something, which is one everyday sense of reason.

clue.text: Erase, clearing out webpage describing rules of on-line communication

indicators.note: clearing out the contents empties a word, leaving only its outside letters
to describe a shape is to draw round it, so one piece surrounds the other

blocks.note: the outer letters of webpage
IP, Internet Protocol, is the set of rules for sending data online

explanation.surface: Deleting a website page that sets out internet etiquette.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rules of on-line communication' suggests netiquette, but it is the abbreviation for Internet Protocol.
explanation.definitionFit: To wipe a disk or recording is to erase its contents completely.

clue.text: People upset - rogue beaten up

indicators.note: something beaten up is knocked out of shape, so the letters are battered into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A crowd is distressed after a villain gets a thrashing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upset' looks like the anagram signal but is fodder; the signal is 'beaten up' at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: The Portuguese are the people of Portugal, a nationality used here as a plural noun.

clue.text: City skinned Stoke then United lost to you

indicators.note: removing the skin strips away the outside, so the end letters go
what is lost is gone, so a letter is removed

blocks.note: Stoke without its outside letters
U is the abbreviation for United in football team names
the word from which the letter is lost

explanation.surface: A football report: Stoke City were thrashed, then Manchester United lost to your side.
explanation.walkthrough: Stoke City and United are English football clubs, which sells the sporting surface; 'skinned' and 'lost' both mean letters removed.
explanation.definitionFit: Tokyo is the capital city of Japan, a plain example of the category.

clue.text: What comes before foxtrot is recorded in dance choreography

indicators.note: something recorded in a document is written inside it, so the letters lie within the words

blocks.note: the letters span the end of the first word and start of the second

explanation.surface: A dance routine notation showing which step precedes the foxtrot.
explanation.walkthrough: The foxtrot is a ballroom dance, but here it is the NATO phonetic word for F, and the one before is E's.
explanation.definitionFit: In the NATO phonetic alphabet, Echo stands for E and Foxtrot for F, so it comes immediately before.

clue.text: Local administrator regenerated empty canal network

indicators.note: an empty word has lost its contents, leaving only its outside letters
regeneration rebuilds something in a new form, so the letters are remade into another order

blocks.note: the outer letters of canal
taken as written

explanation.surface: A council official revives a disused canal system, as in an urban renewal scheme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Regenerated' sits by the official as if describing urban renewal, but it rearranges CL and the network.
explanation.definitionFit: A town clerk was the official in charge of the records and administration of a British town council.

clue.text: Tacks north and south to circumvent trouble

indicators.note: to circumvent literally means to go round, so two pieces surround the middle

blocks.note: N is the abbreviation for north
to ail is to trouble, as in 'what ails you'
S is the abbreviation for south

explanation.surface: A sailboat changes course up and down the coast to avoid difficulties.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tacks' plays on sailing, as do north and south; the definition is the noun for small nails.
explanation.definitionFit: Tacks are short sharp nails with broad heads, so they are a kind of nail.

clue.text: Instrument connected with catching orca primarily

definitions.text: Instrument connected with catching orca primarily

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so only the first letter is taken
catching something means holding it, so one piece is held inside another

blocks.note: a harp is a musical instrument
a phone or power line that is connected is on
the first letter of orca

explanation.surface: A description of a tool used by whalers to capture a killer whale.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue doubles as the definition: a harpoon is just such a device. 'Instrument' also means a musical one in the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A harpoon is a barbed spear thrown or fired to catch whales and other large sea creatures.

clue.text: Limitless rules restricting game go too far

indicators.note: without limits a word loses its boundaries, its first and last letters
restricting something hems it in, so one piece is enclosed by the other

blocks.note: to rule is to govern
RU is Rugby Union

explanation.surface: Unlimited regulations constraining a sport are excessive.
explanation.walkthrough: RU stands for rugby union, a game in crosswords; it goes inside GOVERNS once G and S are trimmed.
explanation.definitionFit: To overrun is to exceed a limit or time allowed, as when a meeting goes on too long.
